bugs.title: Fan toggles far exceed 2-per-5s limit on button activity
bugs.description: The boost branch at lines 62-67 calls driveFan(true) on every 50 ms sample while D4 reads LOW, with no debounce and no tracking of prior state, so each press/bounce edge re-drives the fan and the release lets the temperature logic drive it back. Measured evidence shows D5 toggled 7 times in a 5000 ms window (bounce), 8 times (short clean presses) and 26 times (rapid presses), all far above the limit of 2. There is no rate limiter or minimum dwell time anywhere in driveFan (lines 29-33) to enforce the 2-toggle cap. D5 toggled 7 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 1.00 s (limit 2), and 8 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

bugs.title: Pump chatters because there is no hysteresis or debounce
bugs.description: The control logic at lines 71-78 uses a single threshold START_CM (45.0) with no stop threshold and no hysteresis band, so any level reading below 45.0 immediately calls setPump(false) and any reading at or above it calls setPump(true). Because sampleLevelCm() (lines 22-24) is read raw every 40 ms with no filtering or debounce, sensor noise and fast swings around the threshold toggle D7 on every poll. The measurements confirm this: 64 toggles in a 5000 ms window during threshold hover, 34 during rapid oscillation, and 8 during a brief glitch spike, all far above the limit of 2. D7 toggled 64 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 1.32 s (limit 2), and 84 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

bugs.title: Blink schedule uses 8-bit millis slice, causing rapid toggling
bugs.description: Line 53 stores millis() into a uint8_t (nowSlice) and line 61 compares (uint8_t)(nowSlice - lastSlice) >= HALF_MS, so the elapsed-time counter wraps every 256 ms instead of measuring true 500 ms intervals. This makes the beacon toggle far faster than the intended 500 ms half-period, producing the measured 8 toggles in a 2000 ms window (limit 5) and 16 toggles over the 8.00 s run. The same 8-bit truncation at lines 46 and 59 compounds the error across quiet-hold and rollover scenarios. D12 toggled 8 times in a 2000 ms window starting at 245 ms (limit 5), and 16 times over the whole 8.00 s run.
